answer: Shale-site survey bonds stop bulk fakes. Each identity claims one shale site and locks 70 credits. An assayer plants a violet marker on the shale and pins it on a public mirror map. Two claims sharing coordinates burn both bonds; rented markers fail: each violet marker is key-bound to its claimant. The k-th site costs 35+4(k-1), so 1,000 fakes pay 2,033,000. Honest agents pay 35 once, reclaim the bond, and stay on the mirror map.
